note: Weekly target = September monthly GA4 target × 3/30 plus October monthly GA4 target × 4/30, because the week straddles the two months: 28, 29 and 30 September fall in September and 1 to 4 October in October. That gives a blended weekly target of 977. Hong Kong booked 913 GA4 bookings, 6.6 percent behind, down 6.8 percent week on week and down 4.7 percent year on year. Three of six venues beat the weekly target. Cantina (+53.0 percent) and Shiro (+23.8 percent) led it, with The Chinese Library (+22.9 percent) also ahead. The three behind are Dim Sum Library (−23.6 percent), Hutong HK (−23.1 percent) and Aqua HK (−20.9 percent). The shortfall is concentrated in the two largest venues. Aqua HK fell to 178 from 229 even though users rose 7.9 percent to 3,924, so the fall is conversion, not traffic: 4.5 percent against 6.3 percent the week before. Hutong HK fell to 213 from 277; its National Day firework dinner page drew 469 sessions and produced one website booking, so it is still reading as a content page rather than a booking page. The year-on-year comparison is a hard one: the same week last year carried the 1 October National Day holiday and the Golden Week inbound run, and Aqua HK alone booked 229 then. Year to date the portfolio is 6.5 percent ahead of target, and Aqua HK (−5.8 percent) and Dim Sum Library (−8.8 percent) remain the only two venues behind on the financial year line. Shiro is shown as two sites: Shiro Pacific Place booked 79 and Shiro Tai Kwun 77. Together that is the 156 measured against Shiro’s combined target of 126. Tai Kwun opened in 2026, so it has no year-on-year comparison. Below the portfolio line, outside the target set: Vesu booked 83 against 73 the week before and 70 in the same week last year, and The Canton Library, open since 8 September, booked 27 against 46. Neither is in the portfolio total or its variance.
outside_label: Outside the target set: not in the portfolio total or its variance
foot_extra: Shiro’s weekly target of 126 (YTD 4,259) covers both sites, so the two Shiro rows carry no individual target and are measured together on the “Shiro, both sites” row. Shiro’s Meta and Google accounts are shared by both sites, so Shiro ad spend is shown once on that row and never split. The Canton Library’s cost per booking leaves out its awareness campaign spend; its Google Ads account still has no working booking conversion. Targets for Vesu and The Canton Library are not set yet.
